spec.summary: Vlogs, tutorials, reviews and travel Reels are narrated, and today a creator has to record the voice in another app, export it, and import the file as a sound clip, then line it up by ear. 209 adds **voice-over recording**: arm a Voice track, press Record, watch the video play from the playhead after a short count-in, and talk; when you stop, the take is an ordinary sound clip (208) on that Voice track, in sync with the picture it was spoken over, with its waveform, fades, volume and keyframes, and it counts as voice for ducking. A take recorded over part of an earlier one replaces just that part (punch-in), so a fluffed sentence is re-recorded without redoing the rest. The microphone is chosen and checked with a live level meter, is open only while the recording controls are open, and nothing leaves the device. It works the same in the browser and in the desktop app (which today refuses every microphone request, and the web app's headers forbid the microphone).

US-1.text: As a vlogger, I want to talk over my video while I watch it play, so that my narration matches what is on screen without lining it up by hand.

US-2.text: As a creator who fluffed one sentence, I want to re-record just that part, so that I don't have to record the whole narration again.

US-3.text: As a creator, I want to choose my microphone and see how loud I am before and while I record, so that my voice is neither too quiet nor clipped.

US-4.text: As a privacy-minded user, I want the microphone to be on only while I'm recording, with a clear sign that it is, and my voice to stay on my device.

US-5.text: As a creator, I want a take I recorded to behave like any other sound clip (edit, fade, duck the music under it, undo, save, export), and not to lose it if the tab or app closes mid-take.

US-6.text: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want to arm, start, stop and check a recording without a mouse and hear what is happening (the count-in, recording, the take's length).

AC-1.text: **Record voice** (in the Audio panel and on each Voice track's header, Q1) records onto a Voice track: the one whose button was used, else the selected Voice track, else the first Voice track; with no Voice track one named **Voice** is added (refused with the reason when there are already 8 audio tracks). Pressing Record starts a count-in (3 s by default; Off, 3 or 5 s, Q4), then the preview plays from the playhead and the microphone records until **Stop**, the end of the video, or a take length of 60 min (Q5, Q7). The take becomes one sound clip that starts on the timeline at the playhead's position when recording began and is as long as the recording, within 20 ms, named “Voice 1”, “Voice 2” … in recording order. Cancelling during the count-in records nothing.

AC-2.text: **Punch-in** (Q2): where a take overlaps sound clips on the track it was recorded on, the overlapped parts are removed (a clip fully covered is deleted, one partly covered is trimmed, one that covers the whole take is split around it), so the track never holds overlapping clips (208 AC-2). Other tracks are untouched. The take and these changes are **one undo step**: undo restores the earlier clips exactly and removes the take; redo puts it back.

AC-3.text: **Sync**: a word spoken while a frame is on screen lands on that frame in the take. The take is placed using the input and output latency the browser reports, plus a **Recording offset** of −250 to +250 ms (0 by default) remembered per microphone (Q10). For a fixture with a known reported latency and a simulated input delayed by it, the take's start is within 5 ms of the true position. (A clap test on real hardware, within one frame at 30 fps, is a deferred manual check.)

AC-4.text: **Microphone choice and level**: the recording controls list the microphones (the system default first; names once permission is given) and remember the choice per device; unplugging the chosen one falls back to the default and says so. A **level meter** shows the input's peak in dBFS at least 20 times a second while the controls are open, whether or not recording, and marks **Too loud** for 2 s after a peak at or above −1 dBFS. **Voice clean-up** (the browser's echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain, off by default, Q6) is one switch, remembered per device. For a fixture of tone bursts at known levels the meter's readings are within 0.5 dB.

AC-5.text: **Hearing the video while recording** (Q3): by default the picture plays with its sound muted, so speakers aren't recorded into the take; **Hear the video (use headphones)** plays the preview's mix while recording. The track being recorded onto is never played back during the take.

AC-6.text: **Every failure is explained, and nothing recorded is lost**: microphone permission refused (how to allow it in the browser or in the system settings on desktop), no microphone, the microphone in use by another app, not a secure page (web on plain http), recording not supported by the browser, and the microphone unplugged or failing mid-take. Each shows a message with the reason and what to do, is logged with `logError('handled', …)`, and leaves the project unchanged, except that a take cut short by a failure keeps everything recorded up to it and says so (“Voice 3 kept: 41.2 s, the microphone stopped”).

AC-7.text: **The microphone is open only while it is needed**: it is opened when the recording controls are opened (for the level meter) and every input track is stopped within 1 s of closing them, leaving the video workspace or the tab being hidden while not recording. While recording, a red **Recording** sign with the elapsed time shows on the stage and the timeline. The recording is stored only on the device, as imported sound files are, and sent nowhere. The web app's Permissions-Policy allows the microphone for its own page only (camera, geolocation and payment stay off), and the desktop app grants microphone access only to its own page and only for audio: a request for the camera, the screen or from any other origin is refused (Q12).

AC-8.text: **A take is an ordinary sound clip**: it has its waveform (208 AC-4), can be moved, trimmed, split, faded, keyframed and deleted like any sound clip, counts as voice for ducking on Music and Effects tracks (208 AC-6, updated within 1 s of the take ending), is saved with the project and found again after a reload or reopening the desktop app, and is in the export. Its file is a format the app's sound import accepts (Q7) and is kept as the project's own media (408: `keepMedia(file, true)`, copied into the browser's project storage, or into `library/media/` in the desktop app), so it is there whenever the project is reopened, and deleting the last project that uses it frees it.

AC-9.text: **Crash safety** (Q8): while recording, the take is saved to the device at least once a second. If the tab or app closes, crashes or loses power mid-take, the next time the project is opened it offers “Recover voice recording (Voice 3, 41 s, recorded 19 Oct 14:02)”: **Add to the timeline** places it where it was being recorded (with punch-in, one undo step) and **Discard** deletes it. At most the last 2 s are lost. Recordings not recovered or discarded within 30 days are deleted.

AC-10.text: Every control is reachable and works from the keyboard: Record / Stop with a key in the video workspace (Shift + R, Q11) as well as the buttons, Esc cancels a count-in. Screen readers hear the count-in (“Recording in 3, 2, 1”), the start (“Recording on Voice”), a Too loud warning at most once every 5 s, and the result (“Voice 2 added at 0:12.4, 8.6 s; replaced 2.1 s of Voice 1”). axe finds no violations with the recording controls open and while recording. (Proven in 290 with Playwright's fake microphone.)

AC-11.text: Recording works the same in the browser (Chromium, Firefox, Safari where they can record, on desktop and phone layouts) and in the desktop app on Windows and macOS (Constitution V): in an end-to-end test with a fake media stream, a 5 s take is recorded, lands at the playhead, plays in the preview and is in the exported MP4's sound within 20 ms of where it was placed. On macOS the desktop app asks for the system's microphone permission the first time and says how to allow it in System Settings when it was refused. (Proven in 290.)

AC-12.text: Recording does not slow the preview: while recording a 10-minute take over a 1080p 30 fps project on the reference laptop, the preview drops no more frames than when playing without recording (within 1 %), memory grows by at most 20 MB for the take, and the entry chunk stays ≤ 350 KB (the recording code loads with `import()` when the controls are first opened). (Measured in 290.)

AC-13.text: `docs/MEDIA-STUDIO.md` (recording, punch-in, microphone, sync offset, privacy, recovery, keys, limits), `docs/DESKTOP.md` (the microphone permission on Windows and macOS), `specs/lld.md` (the recorder, the latency placement, the permission rules), `CHANGELOG.md` and the in-app docs describe the change; the media studio's “Still to do” no longer lists voice-over recording.

Q1.text: Where are the recording controls? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ a **Record voice** section in the Audio panel (microphone, meter, count-in, clean-up, offset, Record) plus a record button on each Voice track's header that opens it with that track chosen. No separate recording screen.

Q2.text: What happens when a take overlaps earlier sound on its track? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ punch-in: the take replaces the overlapped parts (trim, split or delete, one undo step), as in audio editors, so re-recording a sentence is one take. Alternatives: refuse to start where the track isn't free, or put the take on a new track. Overlap is checked only on the track recorded onto.

Q3.text: Should the video's sound play while recording? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ muted by default (laptop speakers would be recorded into the take and the ducking would treat them as voice); a switch **Hear the video (use headphones)** plays the mix, still without the track being recorded.

Q4.text: Count-in and pre-roll? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ a count-in of Off / 3 s (default) / 5 s, shown on the stage, with no sound (no beeps, which would be recorded). No pre-roll (playing a few seconds before the punch-in point) in 209: it would need the take to start later than playback; it can come later.

Q5.text: When does recording stop by itself? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ at the end of the video (the preview stops there and sound past the end isn't heard, 208 Q6), at 60 min, or on a failure. It does **not** stop at the next clip on the track: punch-in (Q2) replaces it, which the result announcement reports.

Q6.text: The browser's own voice processing (echo cancellation, noise suppression, automatic gain)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ off by default, because it dulls the voice and pumps the level, and creators usually record with the speakers muted (Q3); one switch **Voice clean-up** turns all three on for people recording on laptop speakers or in noisy rooms. Noise removal of our own is out of scope (a later item).

Q7.text: What format and limits? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ whatever the browser records natively that our sound import accepts: Opus in WebM on Chromium, Electron and Firefox, AAC in MP4 on Safari, mono, at the microphone's rate; up to 60 min per take (about 60 MB at 128 kb/s, under 208's 100 MB per sound file). No re-encoding to WAV (it would be 10× larger and the export re-encodes to AAC anyway). **Add sound also accepts WebM** (`.webm` / `.weba`; the maintainer, 2026-10-20), so a take saved with **Save as file** (or any WebM sound) can be added again; a WebM without a duration in its header (MediaRecorder writes none) is measured from its packets, as a take is.

Q8.text: Crash recovery for a take in progress? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ yes: chunks saved to the device every second (IndexedDB on the web, the data folder on desktop), offered on next open, deleted after 30 days if ignored. A long narration lost to a crash is the worst failure this feature can have.

Q9.text: Takes and take lanes (keeping every attempt and choosing between them)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ out of scope for 209: the replaced take is gone except through undo. Take lanes are a later item if people ask.

Q10.text: How is sync made right? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ automatically from the latencies the browser reports (the audio context's output and base latency and the input's own latency where available), plus a manual **Recording offset** of −250 to +250 ms per microphone for hardware the browser misreports (Bluetooth headsets). A guided clap-test calibration is out of scope.

Q11.text: Which key starts and stops recording? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ Shift + R in the video workspace (R alone is free today but is a common single-key tool in editors, so it is left for later); Space still plays and pauses and, while recording, stops the take as well.

Q12.text: How far do the permission changes go? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ web: `Permissions-Policy` becomes `microphone=(self)`, camera, geolocation and payment stay `()`. Desktop: the permission handlers grant `media` only when the request comes from the app's own `app://chitthi` page and asks for audio only; video, screen capture and every other origin are refused, as now. macOS: the app declares a microphone usage description and asks the system for access on first use. Windows uses its own privacy setting, which we explain when access fails.

Q13.text: Does recording work on phones (the web app's phone layout)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ yes, with the same controls in the Audio panel; the phone project of the e2e tests covers it in 290. Recording with the screen locked or the tab in the background is not supported (the browser pauses it): the take stops and keeps what was recorded (AC-6).

Q14.text: Agent tools for recording? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ none: an agent can't speak into the microphone; agent tools for audio belong to 212.

sections.title: Non-Functional Requirements
sections.markdown:
- **Performance:** recording never blocks or slows the timeline or the preview (AC-12); the recorder code loads with `import()` when the recording controls are first opened, so the entry chunk stays ≤ 350 KB; a take is written to the device as it is recorded, not held in memory.
- **Accuracy:** a take is placed within 20 ms of where it was recorded (AC-1), within 5 ms of the true position given the reported latency (AC-3); the meter is within 0.5 dB (AC-4).
- **Privacy and security:** the microphone is open only while the recording controls are open or a take is recording (AC-7); nothing is uploaded; only the app's own page may use the microphone, and only for audio, on web and desktop (Q12); any new IPC message goes through `electron/ipc.cjs` and validates its arguments; the CSP stays as strict (no new hosts).
- **Reliability:** a failure mid-take keeps what was recorded (AC-6); a crash loses at most the last 2 s (AC-9).
- **Accessibility:** every control works from the keyboard and is announced; axe passes (AC-10).
- **Compatibility:** web and desktop alike (Constitution V); no new dependency (the browser's own recording and Web Audio); every existing project opens and exports unchanged.
- **Free and open source:** recording is for everyone, on the web and in the desktop app.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.markdown:
- Take lanes / keeping every attempt (Q9); pre-roll before the punch-in point (Q4); a guided sync calibration (Q10).
- Our own noise removal, EQ, compression or other voice effects (Q6); speech-to-text and captions (Phase 3).
- Recording the camera, the screen or system sound; several microphones at once; stereo recording.
- Recording in the photo studio or the print studio.
- Agent tools for recording (Q14).

risks.text: **R1 MediaRecorder WebM has no duration** (Chrome writes a live stream: `<audio>` reports Infinity, which 208's `soundIO.length` rejects). Mitigation: measure with Mediabunny `computeDuration()` (§6); spike task T001 records 5 s in Chrome, Electron, Firefox and Safari and checks that the joined blob plays, scans, mixes in the export and reports its length within 20 ms. If Mediabunny can't read one browser's output, decode it with `decodeAudioData` on the window instead.

**R2 Chunk joining and crash recovery** (Safari's fragmented MP4 joined from timeslices; a WebM cut mid-cluster after a crash). Mitigation: the spike also kills a recording mid-way (page reload) and checks the recovered blob decodes up to its last whole chunk; if a format can't be recovered, that browser gets recovery of finished takes only, and AC-9 says so (spec changelog).

**R3 Sync accuracy** varies with hardware and browsers that misreport latency (Bluetooth). Mitigation: the manual Recording offset (Q10); the clap test in 290 on the maintainer's laptop with the built-in microphone and a USB one; if the reported latency makes it worse anywhere, fall back to 0 there.

**R4 IndexedDB in unit tests** (Node has none). Mitigation: `takeStore` behind an interface with an in-memory implementation for tests; the IndexedDB part is thin and checked by the spike and by 290's e2e (reload mid-take). No new devDependency (D3, chosen 2026-10-19).

**R5 macOS microphone permission under the hardened runtime**: without the audio-input entitlement the system silently returns silence. Mitigation: entitlement + `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` in this feature; checked on the maintainer's Mac in 290 (AC-11). Unsigned builds still ask (the prompt names the app).

**R6 Phones**: mobile browsers pause recording in the background and may switch the audio route (speaker to earpiece) when the microphone opens. Mitigation: the track-ended path keeps the take (AC-6); 290's phone project; documented.

Pure functions and the recorder with injected IO and a fake clock are unit / integration tested; e2e (fake microphone), the clap test and the timing run are listed in 290 (D-033).
Browser APIs (getUserMedia, MediaRecorder, AnalyserNode, IndexedDB) and Mediabunny, already shipped. No new dependency (R4 keeps `fake-indexeddb` optional).
Decisions D1–D3 go to `memory/decisions.md` when approved; spike findings to `learnings.md`.

constitution.principle: V. Free and Open Source, Always
constitution.notes: Recording is the same on web and desktop; no limits differ.

constitution.principle: VI. On the User's Device, No Backend
constitution.notes: Takes are stored only in the device's IndexedDB; no network call is added.

constitution.principle: VIII. What You See Is What You Get
constitution.notes: A take is an ordinary sound clip through 208's single gain chain for preview and export; the recorder only produces the file and its place.
No IPC added. The permission predicate is narrowed to audio from `app://chitthi`; everything else stays refused; sandbox and fuses unchanged.

Record voice is `lazy()`-loaded (entry ≤ 350 KB, checked by `npm run build`); keyboard, live-region announcements and axe (AC-10 in 290); meter has a text value; reduced motion: the count-in is numbers, no animation.

constitution.principle: XI. Agents Use the Same Code
constitution.notes: No agent tool (Q14, accepted: an agent can't speak into a microphone). A recorded take is an ordinary sound clip, so 212's audio tools will reach it.

sections.title: Approach
sections.markdown:
Today a voice can only come in as a file (208's **Add sound**). 209 adds a recorder that turns the microphone into the same thing: a `VSound` with a `Blob` and an object URL, placed on a Voice track by a pure engine function and committed with one `change()` (one undo step). Everything after the take ends (waveform, ducking, edits, export) is 208's code, unchanged. The browser's own pieces do the hard parts: `getUserMedia` for the microphone, `MediaRecorder` for encoding (Opus in WebM, AAC in MP4 on Safari, Q7), an `AnalyserNode` for the meter. No new dependency. Under D-033 every task is proven by unit tests on pure functions and on the recorder with injected fakes; the fake-microphone e2e, the clap test and the timing run go to 290.

**§1 Where a take goes (`engine/voiceTake.ts`, AC-1).** `recordTarget(tracks, chosen, selected)` picks the Voice track (the button's, else the selected Voice track, else the first Voice track) or adds one named **Voice** with role Voice (`addAudioTrack` + `setAudioTrack`), or returns 208's eight-track refusal. `takeName(sounds)` is “Voice N”, N one more than the highest “Voice N” already in the project. `canRecord(video)` refuses with the reason when the video is empty, the playhead is at its end, or the track is locked.

**§2 Punch-in (`engine/soundClips.ts`, AC-2).** `punchIn(audio, track, start, end, ctx)` clears `[start, end)` on one track: a clip inside it is deleted, one overlapping an edge is trimmed (its keys stay on the same sound, as `trimSound` does), one covering the whole span is split around it (`splitKeys`), a `toEnd` clip is first turned into a fixed length (as `moveSound` does past the end). `placeTake(audio, tracks, take, start, track, ctx)` = `punchIn` + the take on exactly that track, never another; it returns the new clips and what was replaced (seconds per clip name) for the announcement. Pure, so AC-2 is a unit test, and one `change('', { sounds, tracks })` makes the take, the punch-in and a new Voice track one undo step.

**§3 Sync (`engine/voiceTake.ts`, AC-3).** The preview's clock is wall time: `usePlayback` (VideoStage.tsx) maps `performance.now()` to the playhead from a `(startTime, startWall)` pair. Recording starts playback from the recorder's `start` event, and the recorder reads that pair (§5). `takeStart({ playStart, playWall, captureWall, inputLatency, offset })` returns the timeline second of the take's first sample: the playhead at the moment capture began, minus the input latency (the microphone hears a word that much before the recorder gets it), plus the user's **Recording offset** (−250 to +250 ms, per microphone, Q10). Output latency matters only for the video's sound, which is muted by default (Q3), and the picture is drawn in the same frame as the playhead, so the input side is what is compensated. `inputLatency` comes from the track's `getSettings().latency` where the browser reports it, else the audio context's `baseLatency`, else 0. The take's length is measured from its file (§6), not the wall clock, and checked against it (within 20 ms, AC-1).

**§4 The microphone (`lib/microphone.ts`, `engine/voiceLevel.ts`, AC-4, AC-5).** `lib/microphone.ts` wraps `navigator.mediaDevices`: `listMicrophones()` (default first), `openMicrophone(deviceId, cleanUp)` (audio only, mono; `echoCancellation`, `noiseSuppression`, `autoGainControl` all equal to the **Voice clean-up** switch, Q6), `onDevicesChanged()`, and `micFailure(error)` mapping `NotAllowedError`, `NotFoundError`, `NotReadableError`, `SecurityError` / no secure context, and a missing `MediaRecorder` to the messages of AC-6 (desktop: “Allow Chitthi Studio under Privacy → Microphone in System Settings” on macOS, “Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone” on Windows). The meter is an `AnalyserNode` on its own `AudioContext`; `engine/voiceLevel.ts` has `peakDbfs(samples)` and `tooLoud(history, now)` (≥ −1 dBFS, held 2 s) as pure functions, read at least 20 times a second (a rAF loop throttled to 30 Hz). Choices (microphone, clean-up, count-in, offset per microphone, Hear the video) are saved in `localStorage` (`chitthi.voice`, try/catch) and validated on read.

**§5 The recorder (`state/voiceRecorder.ts`, AC-1, AC-5–AC-7).** A small store (`useSyncExternalStore`, like the others, no undo) with phases `closed → ready → countIn → recording → finishing`, and the current level, elapsed time and message. Its IO is injected (`recorderIO`: microphone, `MediaRecorder` maker, clock, timers, the take store), so unit tests drive it with fakes, time as input (Constitution II). `openControls(track)` opens the microphone for the meter (AC-7); `closeControls()`, leaving the workspace, and `visibilitychange` to hidden while not recording stop every input track at once (well under 1 s). `record()` runs the count-in (Off / 3 / 5 s, Esc or Stop cancels with nothing recorded), then `recorder.start(1000)`, and on its `start` event sets `recording` in the video store and starts playback (§3). It stops on Stop / Shift + R / Space, when playback reaches the end of the video (`playing` turns false), at 60 min, or when the track ends (unplugged, background tab on a phone, Q13), keeping what was recorded (AC-6). Then §6, §2, one `change()`, `scanMedia()` (208's waveform and ducking scan) and the announcement.

**§6 Takes on the device (`lib/takeStore.ts`, AC-8, AC-9, D1, re-read against 408).** A take **in progress** is kept for crash recovery only: each `dataavailable` chunk (every second) is appended to IndexedDB, database `chitthi-takes` (its own, so `chitthi`'s version doesn't change), store `takes`: `{ id, name, startedAt, track, start, mime, chunks: Blob[], done }`. In the desktop app this IndexedDB lives in the pinned data folder (`%APPDATA%\Chitthi`, Q8), so no new IPC is needed. On stop the chunks are joined into one `Blob`; its length is the decoded length (Mediabunny's `Input.computeDuration()` misses the last packet in WebM: 60 ms on Chromium, 20 ms on Firefox, T001) (MediaRecorder's WebM has no duration header, so the `<audio>` element reads Infinity: R1), which also proves the file decodes before it is placed. The finished take is then kept as the project's own media with 408's `keepMedia(file, true)` (owned: copied into OPFS in the browser, written into `library/media/<id>` on desktop) before `addTake()` places it, and its entry in `chitthi-takes` is deleted once the clip is on the timeline: from then on the project (408's autosave) holds it. A full disk (`QuotaExceededError`, or the media store's 'no room') keeps the take on the timeline in memory and says it can't be kept. Takes in progress older than 30 days are deleted when the store opens. Recovery of an interrupted take: AC-9, D1.

**§7 The preview while recording (`state/videoStore.ts`, `components/studio/VideoStage.tsx`, `previewSound.ts`, AC-5).** `VState.recording: { track: string; hear: boolean } | null` (not saved, not undone, leaves the last export current). `soundsAt` skips the recorded track while `recording` is set, and the stage sets the master gain to 0 unless `hear`. `usePlayback` writes its `(startTime, startWall)` to `playClock` in the store, which the recorder reads (§3). The **Recording** sign (red dot, elapsed time, `role="status"`) shows on the stage and on the track's row.

**§8 The UI (`components/studio/RecordVoice.tsx`, `AudioPanel.tsx`, `TrackHead.tsx`, `VideoWorkspace.tsx`, AC-1, AC-10, AC-12).** A **Record voice** group in the Audio panel (Q1), loaded with `lazy()` so the recorder and the meter stay out of every other chunk: microphone menu, meter (a bar with −60…0 dBFS, Too loud), Voice clean-up, Hear the video (use headphones), count-in (Off / 3 / 5 s), Recording offset, the target track, **Record** / **Stop**, and the messages. Voice tracks' headers get a record button that opens the Audio panel with that track chosen. VideoWorkspace's key handler gets Shift + R (record / stop) and Esc (cancel a count-in); Space stops a take (Q11). Announcements go through 208's `tell()` live region (AC-10's wording, Too loud at most every 5 s).

**§9 Permissions (`nginx/security-headers.conf`, `electron/permissions.cjs`, `electron/main.cjs`, `electron-builder.yml`, `build/entitlements.mac.plist`, AC-7, AC-11).** Web: `microphone=(self)`; camera, geolocation and payment stay `()` (vite preview reads the CSP from the same file; it is changed to send the Permissions-Policy too, so e2e sees it: T001 found it sends only the CSP). Desktop: the request and check handlers move into a new `electron/permissions.cjs` with one pure predicate, `allowed(permission, details, appOrigin)`: today's two permissions, plus `media` only when the requesting origin is `app://chitthi` and the media types are exactly `['audio']` (the check handler: `mediaType === 'audio'`). On macOS the request handler first asks the system (`systemPreferences.getMediaAccessStatus('microphone')`, `askForMediaAccess`), and the build adds `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` (`mac.extendInfo`) and the `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement, which the hardened runtime needs. No IPC handler is added. The new file goes into `files:` in `electron-builder.yml`. The CSP needs nothing: `media-src 'self' blob:` already covers playing the takes.

**§10 Docs (AC-13).** `docs/MEDIA-STUDIO.md` (Record voice section, keys, limits, privacy, recovery; “Still to do” drops voice-over), `docs/DESKTOP.md` (microphone permission on Windows and macOS), `specs/lld.md` (recorder phases, placement formula, take store, permission predicate), `CHANGELOG.md`, the in-app docs (`src/data/docs.ts`).

sections.title: Data Structures & Interfaces
Techniques
sections.markdown:
- **MediaRecorder with a 1 s timeslice** (`start(1000)`): each `dataavailable` chunk is appended to IndexedDB at once, so a crash loses at most the chunk in flight (≤ 2 s, AC-9). The chunks of one recording joined in order form a valid file (WebM clusters; Safari's fragmented MP4): R2's spike checks both. MIME: the first of `audio/webm;codecs=opus`, `audio/mp4;codecs=mp4a.40.2`, `audio/mp4` that `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported` accepts, at 128 kb/s mono.
- **Length and decodability from Mediabunny** (already shipped, MPL-2.0, loaded with `import()`): `Input.computeDuration()` on the joined blob. If it can't read the file, the take is kept as a recovery entry with “couldn't be read” and **Save as file** (nothing recorded is lost, AC-6).
- **Placement** is the pure `takeStart` (§3) fed by one clock: `performance.now()` for both playback and the recorder's `start` event. The `start` event fires when capture begins, so the wall time read there is the take's sample 0.
- **No audio thread**: the meter reads an `AnalyserNode` (`getFloatTimeDomainData`, 2048 samples) on the main thread at 30 Hz; MediaRecorder encodes off the main thread. Nothing runs per sample in JavaScript, so the preview isn't slowed (AC-12).
- **Releasing the microphone**: every path out (close, leave, hidden tab, failure, unmount) goes through one `release()` that stops each `MediaStreamTrack` and closes the meter's context; the browser's own recording indicator goes out with it (AC-7).
- **Security**: the desktop predicate checks the requesting origin and the exact media types; `getUserMedia` for video, `getDisplayMedia`, and every other origin stay refused. No IPC, no new host, no CSP change.

sections.title: Decisions for the maintainer
sections.markdown:
**D1 Video projects aren't saved, so what happens to takes after a reload?** The spec's AC-8 says a take is “saved with the project and found again after a reload … an exported `.chitthi` project carries it”, and AC-9 offers recovery “the next time the project is opened”. The video studio has no project saving today (the document shape and validator exist; nothing writes or opens a video project), so after a reload the timeline is empty and every clip is gone. Imported files are still on the user's disk; a recorded voice exists nowhere else.
- **A (recommended):** keep every take, finished or interrupted, in the take store for 30 days. The Record voice group lists **Recent recordings** that aren't on the current timeline (name, length, when), each with **Add to the timeline** (at the time it was recorded, on a Voice track, with punch-in, one undo step), **Save as file** (`.webm` / `.m4a`) and **Delete**. An interrupted take is marked “stopped early”. AC-8's reload sentence becomes “stays on the timeline while the project is open; after a reload it is in Recent recordings”, and the `.chitthi` clause is dropped (it comes with project saving). AC-9 keeps its numbers.
- **B:** keep only interrupted takes (as the spec has it); finished takes are lost on reload like the rest of the project; a **Save as file** button in the sound inspector.
- **C (chosen by the maintainer, 2026-10-19):** video and photo projects are saved and reopened, as a feature of their own (408, spec to write) that 209 builds on. A take is then saved with its project like any sound; the take store keeps only takes in progress for crash recovery (AC-9 as written). AC-8 stays as written once 408 defines what “the project” is; its `.chitthi` clause follows 408’s answer on project files.

**Re-read against 408 (2026-10-19, 408 T111):** projects now autosave with their media (408). A finished take is kept as owned media (`keepMedia(file, true)`) and saved with the project; the take store holds takes in progress only, for AC-9's recovery; AC-8's `.chitthi` clause is dropped until project files exist (409).

**D2 Where takes are stored on desktop.** Q8 says “the data folder on desktop”. **Recommended:** the renderer's IndexedDB on both; in the desktop app it lives in the pinned data folder (`%APPDATA%\Chitthi\IndexedDB`), so no new IPC handler or file code is needed. Alternative: files under `userData/takes/` through new IPC (more code, more attack surface, same result). **Chosen by the maintainer (2026-10-19): IndexedDB, as recommended** (D-061).

**D3 Tests for the take store.** **Recommended:** an in-memory implementation behind the same interface for unit tests, the thin IndexedDB part checked by the spike and 290 (R4). Alternative: add `fake-indexeddb` as a devDependency (MIT / Apache-2.0, not bundled). **Chosen by the maintainer (2026-10-19): the in-memory implementation, as recommended** (D-061).

tasks.intro:
**Plan:** `./plan.md`
Legend: `[P]` = can run in parallel with the previous task; 👤 = needs a person. Each task lists files and the proving test.
Test-first: each "failing" task must fail before its paired implementation makes it pass. Tasks run one at a time in the main session.
Tasks are proven by unit tests only (D-033); the fake-microphone e2e, the clap test and the timing run are listed in `290` ("Deferred checks collected from the phase": 209 AC-3, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12).

Record the MIME chosen, the measured lengths and any fallback. Firefox and Safari go to 290.
T001.test: recorded in the result note (no committed test)
notes: **Result (2026-10-19):** Spike passed; no fallback needed. Production build under vite preview (production CSP) in Chromium and Firefox with fake microphones, and the desktop app (app://chitthi, media allowed by a temporary handler): MediaRecorder picks audio/webm;codecs=opus everywhere; 5 s take = 5 chunks (Chromium 72.8 kB, 83 packets of 60 ms; Firefox 250 of 20 ms), decodes at 48 kHz with no console errors. R1: <audio> reads Infinity; Mediabunny computeDuration() is one packet short (4.92 vs 4.98 s decoded on Chromium/Electron, 4.986 vs 4.9935 on Firefox) because the last WebM packet has duration 0, so T032 uses the decoded length (plan §6 updated). R2: reload mid-take, the IndexedDB chunks joined decode (Chromium/Electron 4 chunks 4.02 s, Firefox 6 chunks 5.99 s). Found: vite preview sends only the CSP, not the Permissions-Policy, so T050 also changes vite.config.ts (plan §9 updated). Safari (AAC in MP4) goes to 290. Spike code and hooks removed; findings in memory/learnings.md.
